spec.title: Restaurant Tablet Workflows: Separate Tablets, POS Integration, KDS, and Pickup Screens
spec.audience: restaurant owners, operators, ghost kitchens, quick-service teams, and multi-location managers
spec.problem: Restaurants use tablets in different ways: separate marketplace tablets, POS-integrated ordering, kitchen display screens, pickup screens, self-order kiosks, and customer-facing checkout.
spec.angle: Explain the workflow approaches first, then show where physical mounting still matters even when software integrations reduce tablet count.
spec.comparisonFrame: Mention that POS-native hardware can be best for a single checkout workflow. Aggregator software can reduce tablet count, but restaurants often still need physical screens for pickup, KDS, expo, delivery acceptance, and backup workflows. Locking kiosk-style enclosures are strong for public-facing tablets. iBOLT helps when operators need multi-tablet visibility, wall/counter positioning, and modular mounting across stations.

products.description: The iBOLT Dock'n Lock Tablet Point of Sale Weighted Base Stand is a reliable and secure solution for mounting your 7-10 inch tablet at any checkout counter, kiosk, or point-of-sale system. Designed for businesses that require stability, security, and ease of use, this stand features a locking tablet holder, an adjustable dual ball joint, and a weighted L-bracket base for added balance.
